marks.gloss: money kept out of use and held against the future: the reserve, the deposit, the savings, the cash in the mattress; abstention from spending now
marks.source: Marx, Capital I ch. 3 (hoarding); Keynes, GT ch. 13 (liquidity preference)

marks.gloss: a payment owed later, given now as a claim: the loan, the bond, the IOU, the deposit as the bank's promise; credit from the one side and debt from the other, one relation seen from its two ends
marks.source: Mitchell Innes 1913, 1914; Nietzsche, GM II 4-8; Graeber 2011 ch. 1

marks.gloss: money committed for a return: the loan made to a firm, the share bought, the capital put into a venture; value sent out to come back as more
marks.source: Marx, Capital III ch. 21 (M-M'); Schumpeter 1911 ch. 3

marks.gloss: what comes back beyond the advance: the interest on the loan, the coupon, the dividend, the profit of enterprise, the gain on a sale; read as a share of surplus, the price of time, or the price of parting with liquidity
marks.source: Marx III chs. 21-23; Boehm-Bawerk, Positive Theory book I; Keynes, GT ch. 13

marks.gloss: a promise that can be sold on to a third: the bond, the share certificate, the mortgage bundled and sold; the derivative as a claim on a claim
marks.source: Hilferding 1910 ch. 7; Marx III ch. 29; Appadurai, Banking on Words (2016)

marks.gloss: the present price of an expected stream of payments: the share price, the bond price, a house priced by its rents, a firm priced by its earnings; capitalization, Marx's fictitious capital
marks.source: Marx III chs. 25, 29; Minsky 1986 (the price of capital assets); Nitzan and Bichler 2009

marks.gloss: the promise failed and reckoned: the missed payment, the bankruptcy, the bank run, the crisis; and the cancellation that clears the slate, the jubilee
marks.source: Minsky 1992; Graeber 2011 chs. 1, 12; Vogl, The Specter of Capital (2010)

axioms: A promise can fail; a payment that cannot fail to come is not a promise but a fact.
Money kept breeds nothing; only money parted with returns as more.
A claim on a future stream has a present price, and the price is not the stream.
Credit and debt are one relation seen from its two ends.
A run of promises kept raises the promises made: stability breeds instability.
cast.subject: Finance: the economy's relation to its own future made present: money held against it, money advanced for a return, the promise of payment that is credit from one side and debt from the other, the return that comes back as more, the claim made tradable, the present price of an expected stream, and the reckoning when a promise fails; read from Aristotle, Politics I.8-10; Marx, Capital III part 5; Boehm-Bawerk, Capital and Interest; Keynes, General Theory chs. 12-17; Minsky, Stabilizing an Unstable Economy (1986) and The Financial Instability Hypothesis (1992); Mitchell Innes, What is Money? (1913) and The Credit Theory of Money (1914); Schumpeter, Theory of Economic Development ch. 3; Nietzsche, Genealogy of Morals II; Graeber, Debt (2011); Hilferding, Finance Capital (1910)

premises: The root moment is taken to be money held and money advanced, with the promise as the form a loan takes in the lender's hands; the credit theory (Innes, Ingham) is admitted as a way, the promise passing into the hoard, and the commodity theory is left in open_forks.

Interest is written as the return, the advance in its later moment, without deciding whether it is a share of surplus (Marx), the price of time (Boehm-Bawerk, Fisher) or the price of liquidity (Keynes); the three readings are in open_forks and the return's gloss names them.
Risk and uncertainty are not moments: that a promise can fail is written as an axiom, and the measurable chance of failing is a mark on the promise and the valuation (Knight 1921; Keynes 1937).
Money as a medium of exchange is left at the edge; it appears here only as the hoard (money held) and as the unit in which promises are written (a mark).
Every relation names a way one moment is the next, under Arman's rule of 2026-10-17 as MOLD v6 carries it; words that keep two moments two ('rests on', 'is backed by', 'prices') are in did_not_fit.

Words re-poured on 2026-10-19 at Arman's word (14:0x): a way-word that says only that the one becomes the other ('passes into', 'runs as') is too general and says nothing of HOW; every word must name its channel, the specified path by which the first is the second. So each tuple's word is now its channel, and the signature lists the channels. Moments, glosses, qualities, tuples, polarities, reasons and axioms are unchanged from the pour of 13:4x, which stays in casts/mold-v6_2026-10-19 as the record. derived_check.ordering: by channel, read as directed: hoard -committed-> advance -owed-> promise -honoured-> return -kept-> hoard, a circle; return -committed-> advance; advance -comes back-> return; promise -sold on-> security -priced-> valuation -realized-> return; promise -fails-> default; promise -accepted-> hoard; valuation -counts-> hoard. Refused: the hoard comes back as nothing; the valuation is committed as no advance. Marked derived.

open_forks: Money: a commodity (Menger) or a token of credit and law (Innes, Knapp, Ingham)? Written with the credit theory: the promise passes into the hoard.

Interest: a share of surplus value (Marx), the agio of present over future goods (Boehm-Bawerk, Fisher), or the price of parting with liquidity (Keynes)? The return is written as the advance in its later moment, which all three allow.
Is the default the promise's last moment (written, passes into) or its other side, as the forbearance is the deed's? Kept as a becoming: a promise is not made with its breaking as a side of it.
Whether the state's money and the state's debt are inside (Streeck, Vogl) or at the edge: the state's bond is a promise and is inside; the state's power to tax is distribution's.
Whether the derivative is a moment of its own (Appadurai, Esposito) or the security in a second degree: folded into the security.
Whether 'liquid' is a quality of each moment or a moment of its own (the liquidity; Keynes ch. 17; Mehrling): written as a quality.
did_not_fit: Money as a medium of exchange, the purchase now: the market's, found at the Production-Consumption edge; money appears here only as the hoard and as the unit of account, a mark.
The price of goods: the market's; finance prices claims.
Gambling: a bet with no claim on production; de Goede (2005) shows the line between it and finance is drawn, not found.
Insurance: a promise against loss; a form of the promise, not a moment.
Public finance as revenue: distribution's; the state's debt is a promise and is inside.
The firm's accounting: production's, until the firm is capitalized.

Words left out because each keeps its two moments two: 'rests on' and 'is backed by' (a claim and the asset behind it stay two); 'prices' (the valuation and the claim it prices stay two, so the way is written as the security passing into the valuation); 'funds' (the hoard and what it funds stay two; the way is written as the hoard passing into the advance).

is committed as.meaning: the first, committed for a return, is the second: money kept or come back is sent out as capital. The way the two are one: commitment (the one becomes the other by being committed).

is owed as.meaning: the first, owed back to the one who gave it, is the second: the sum advanced is, in the lender's hands, the claim. The way the two are one: owing (the one becomes the other by being owed).

is honoured as.meaning: the first, honoured, is the second: the promise kept is the payment. The way the two are one: honouring (the one becomes the other by being paid as promised).

comes back as.meaning: the first, having gone out, comes back as the second: the advance returns as more. The way the two are one: the coming-back (the one becomes the other by returning).

is kept as.meaning: the first, kept and not sent out, is the second: the return held is the hoard. The way the two are one: keeping (the one becomes the other by being held).

is sold on as.meaning: the first, sold on to a third, is the second: the promise made transferable is the security. The way the two are one: sale to a third (the one becomes the other by being transferred).

is priced as.meaning: the first, priced by the market, is the second: the security traded is its valuation. The way the two are one: pricing (the one becomes the other by being priced).

is realized as.meaning: the first, sold at its price, is the second: the valuation realized is the return. The way the two are one: realization by sale (the one becomes the other by being sold).

fails as.meaning: the first, unkept, is the second: the promise in its failing is the default. The way the two are one: failing (the one becomes the other by not being kept).

is accepted as.meaning: the first, accepted in payment, is the second: the promise taken as money is money held. The way the two are one: acceptance in payment (the one becomes the other by being taken as money).

counts as.meaning: the first is the second by being counted so, in the books and in the market's reckoning. The way the two are one: counting.

0.reason: money kept becomes money committed when it is lent or invested: the same sum, now out to return as more (Marx, Capital I ch. 3 and II ch. 1: the hoard as the first form of money-capital; Keynes, GT ch. 13 on the choice between holding and lending)

1.reason: what the lender holds after advancing is the claim: the sum advanced is, in the lender's hands, a promise of its repayment (Innes 1914; Marx III ch. 21: the loan returns to its owner as a claim)

2.reason: the claim honoured is the payment with its interest: the promise kept is the return (Boehm-Bawerk, Positive Theory book I; Fisher 1930 ch. 1)

3.reason: the capital advanced comes back as more, M-M': the same value in its later moment (Marx III ch. 21; Schumpeter 1911 ch. 3)

4.reason: the money come back is money held again: the return taken as liquidity (Keynes, GT ch. 13; Marx II ch. 1)

5.reason: the return sent out again is the advance renewed: reinvestment, accumulation (Marx I ch. 24)

6.reason: a claim made transferable is the same claim in a saleable form: the mobilization of capital (Hilferding 1910 ch. 7; Marx III ch. 29)

7.reason: a claim traded has a price, and the price is the claim as the market reads its future: capitalization (Marx III ch. 29; Minsky 1986 ch. 8)

8.reason: a price realized by sale is a return, the capital gain: the speculator's gain from the valuation (Keynes, GT ch. 12; Minsky 1986)

9.reason: the promise unkept is the promise in its failing: the claim become a loss (Minsky 1992; Graeber 2011 ch. 1; Nietzsche GM II 5)

10.reason: a promise taken in payment is held as money: the bank's deposit is its promise and is the money one holds (Innes 1913, 1914; Ingham 2004 ch. 2; Mehrling 2011 ch. 1)

11.reason: money kept breeds nothing: a hoard yields no interest (Aristotle, Politics I.10 1258b, money barren; Keynes, GT ch. 17: money's own yield is nil, its liquidity premium is what holding it costs)

12.reason: a rise in the price of a claim commits no new money to anything: fictitious capital is not capital advanced (Marx III ch. 29: the market value of titles rises and falls with no change in the capital they stand for; Mazzucato 2018 ch. 5)

13.reason: the price of a tradable claim is counted as wealth held, as money would be: the portfolio marked to market stands beside cash on the balance sheet (Marx III ch. 29: the titles counted as capital; Nitzan and Bichler 2009 ch. 9)

marks.gloss: what the making is for, held as a form before the work: the plan of the house, the recipe, the blueprint, the order received; the form in the maker before it is in the matter
marks.source: Aristotle, Metaphysics Z.7 1032b; Marx, Capital I ch. 7 (the architect and the bee)

marks.gloss: the ability to make, had before it is used: the skill, the labour power, the fertility of the land, the machine standing idle; a power of contraries, to make or not
marks.source: Aristotle, Metaphysics Theta.3-8; Marx I ch. 6 (labour power); Georgescu-Roegen 1971 (funds)

marks.gloss: what the work is done on: the ore, the timber, the half-made part, the data set; nature as it enters the making, and past product entering again
marks.source: Marx I ch. 7 (the object of labour); Aristotle, Physics I.7

marks.gloss: the activity itself, purposeful and in time: the hand moving, the pump worked, the code written, the field ploughed
marks.source: Marx I ch. 7; Hegel, PR 196; Arendt 1958 ch. 3

marks.gloss: the working of many as one producer: the pin factory's eighteen operations, the assembly line, the collective worker, the general intellect
marks.source: Smith, WN I.1; Marx I ch. 13; Grundrisse, the fragment on machines

marks.gloss: what stands between the worker and the material and carries past work into the present one: the tool, the machine, the factory, the road; dead labour put to use
marks.source: Marx I chs. 7, 15; Simondon 1958; Sraffa 1960

marks.gloss: what the making leaves: the thing made or the service rendered, the use-value, the harvest, the house; labour objectified, at rest
marks.source: Marx I ch. 7; Hegel, Phenomenology 195; Say, Traite I.1 (utility created)

marks.gloss: what the making leaves beyond what it used up: the harvest beyond the seed and the sowers' food, the net product, surplus value in the capitalist form
marks.source: Quesnay 1758; Sraffa 1960 ch. 2; Marx I ch. 9

marks.gloss: the making again of the conditions of making: the seed kept and sown, the means replaced, the makers fed, raised and rested; the unpaid work of the household
marks.source: Marx I ch. 23; Federici 2004; Bhattacharya ed. 2017

axioms: Nothing is made without being worked: a power unexercised and a plan unexecuted make nothing.
What is made outlasts the making; what is used up in making it does not.
Every making uses up some of what was made before: production is by means of products.
The makers must be made again: there is no production without reproduction.
The surplus is what the making leaves beyond what it used; where there is none, the making only repeats itself.
cast.subject: Production: the making of what is used: a purpose and a capacity to make, work done on a material with instruments, the working of many as one producer, the product that outlasts the act, the surplus beyond what the making used up, and the renewal of the conditions of making; read from Aristotle, NE VI.4, Physics II.3, Metaphysics Theta; Smith, Wealth of Nations I.1-3 and II.3; Hegel, Phenomenology 190-196 and Philosophy of Right 196-198; Marx, Capital I chs. 7, 13-15, 23-24 and the Grundrisse; Quesnay, Tableau (1758); Sraffa, Production of Commodities by Means of Commodities (1960); Schumpeter 1911 ch. 2; Arendt, The Human Condition (1958); Georgescu-Roegen 1971; Federici, Caliban and the Witch (2004)

derived_check.ordering: by channel, read as directed: purpose -carried out-> working; capacity -exercised-> working -fixed-> product -consumed-> reproduction -renewed-> capacity, a circle; working -divided-> cooperation -mechanized-> instrument; product -put to work-> instrument; product -left over-> surplus -invested-> instrument; material -worked into-> product; working -settles-> capacity. Refused: the purpose and the capacity are fixed as no product; the instrument is left over as no surplus. Marked derived.

open_forks: Does the instrument pass into the surplus? Written does-not-hold with Marx; the production function (Wicksteed, Cobb and Douglas) and Sraffa's refusal to attribute the surplus to any factor are the other readings.
Is the mode of production a moment or the frame of all the moments? Carried as the frame; a second caster may admit it as a moment with its ways.
Is innovation (Schumpeter's new combination) a moment of production, or finance's doing through credit? Not written; the entrepreneur has no moment here.
Is nature a co-producer (Moore 2015, ecological economics) or the material only? Written as the material; nature untouched is the edge.
Is a service a product (Say) or an action with no product (Aristotle's praxis, Arendt)? Written as a product; the quality 'lasts beyond the act' carries the difference.
Is cooperation a moment or a quality of the working? Kept as a moment (see premises).
did_not_fit: The sale of the product: the market's, at the Production-Consumption edge.
The distribution of the product and of the means: distribution's; Marx's prior distribution is the contested boundary.
The consumption of the product: consumption's, except productive consumption, which is the reproduction here.
Making money: finance's.
Art as making in the aesthetic sense: adjacent; a product that is not used.
Action (praxis), the other concept of doing: no corner of this run.
Nature untouched: the edge; nature worked is the material.

Words left out because each keeps its two moments two: 'requires' (the working requires the capacity: a condition and what it conditions stay two; the way is written as the capacity passing into the working); 'produces' (the capacity produces the product: a cause and its effect stay two; the way runs through the working); 'belongs to' (the product belongs to the maker: distribution's title, not a way of production); 'is made of' (the product is made of the material: written instead as the material passing into the product, the matter persisting through the form).

is carried out as.meaning: the first, carried out, is the second: the plan in the hands is the working. The way the two are one: execution (the one becomes the other by being carried out).

is exercised as.meaning: the first, exercised, is the second: the power in act is the working. The way the two are one: exercise (the one becomes the other by being exercised).

is worked into.meaning: the first, worked, is the second: the same matter in a new form, the ore in the iron. The way the two are one: working of matter (the one becomes the other by being worked, the matter persisting).

is fixed as.meaning: the first, fixed in a thing, is the second: labour fixes itself in the product. The way the two are one: fixing (the one becomes the other by being fixed in a thing).

is divided as.meaning: the first, divided among many and joined, is the second: the working of many as one producer. The way the two are one: division of labour (the one becomes the other by being divided and joined).

settles as.meaning: the first, repeated, settles as the second: labour settles as skill. The way the two are one: settling by repetition (the one becomes the other by habit).

is mechanized as.meaning: the first, fixed in a mechanism, is the second: the divided working as the machine. The way the two are one: mechanization (the one becomes the other by being built into a mechanism).

is put to work as.meaning: the first, put to work in a further making, is the second: the product as means. The way the two are one: putting to work (the one becomes the other by being used in making).

is consumed as.meaning: the first, consumed to replace what the making used up, is the second: the product as the renewal of the conditions of making. The way the two are one: productive consumption (the one becomes the other by being used up in renewal).

is left over as.meaning: the first, beyond what replaces the used-up, is the second: the product left over is the surplus. The way the two are one: being left over (the one is the other as what remains after replacement).

is invested as.meaning: the first, invested, is the second: the surplus as new means of production. The way the two are one: investment (the one becomes the other by being invested).

is renewed as.meaning: the first, renewing the makers and the means, is the second: reproduction as the capacity to make again. The way the two are one: renewal (the one becomes the other by being made again).

0.reason: the form held in the maker becomes the forming: the plan is realized in the hands (Aristotle, Metaphysics Z.7 1032b; Marx I ch. 7: the result existed ideally at the beginning)

1.reason: the power exercised is the power in act: labour power spent is labour (Aristotle, Metaphysics Theta.6-8; Marx I ch. 7)

2.reason: the stuff worked is the thing made, the same matter in a new form: the ore is the iron, the timber the table (Aristotle, Physics I.7; Marx I ch. 7)

3.reason: the activity, finished, is the thing made: labour objectified, in a state of rest (Hegel, Phenomenology 195; Marx I ch. 7)

4.reason: the working of one, divided and joined with others', is the working of many as one producer (Smith, WN I.1; Marx I ch. 13)

5.reason: labour settles into skill: the worker is made by working, as the just by just acts (Marx I ch. 7: the worker develops the powers that slumber in him; Aristotle NE II.1 by analogy)

6.reason: the divided working, fixed in a mechanism, is the machine: the collective worker's operations objectified (Marx I ch. 15 section 1; Hegel, PR 198)

7.reason: a thing made becomes a means of further making: past labour as dead labour, commodities by means of commodities (Marx I ch. 7; Sraffa 1960 ch. 1)

8.reason: the product used to replace what the making used up is the conditions of making renewed: the seed sown again, the wage that feeds the maker (Marx I ch. 23; Quesnay 1758)

9.reason: the product beyond what replaces the used-up is the surplus: the harvest beyond seed and sustenance, the net product (Quesnay 1758; Sraffa 1960 ch. 2; Marx I ch. 9)

10.reason: the surplus invested is new means of production: accumulation (Marx I ch. 24; Sraffa 1960)

11.reason: the makers fed, raised and rested, and the means replaced, are the capacity to make again (Marx I ch. 23; Federici 2004 ch. 2)

12.reason: a plan is not the thing: the form in the maker becomes the form in the matter only through the making (Aristotle, Metaphysics Z.7; Marx I ch. 7: the architect must build)

13.reason: a power unexercised makes nothing: the builder who does not build has built nothing (Aristotle, Metaphysics Theta.3 against the Megarians; Theta.8)

14.reason: the machine transfers its own worth to the product and adds nothing beyond it; the surplus is the working's, not the means' (Marx I ch. 8; disputed, see open_forks)

marks.gloss: that by which a share is owed to someone: ownership, a contract, membership, need, desert; the entitlement in Nozick's sense, this person's claim to this portion
marks.source: Nozick 1974 ch. 7; Hume, Treatise III.ii.2-4; Locke, Second Treatise ch. 5

marks.gloss: the standard by which shares are right shares: worth, need, equality, contribution, luck; Aristotle's axia, Rawls's difference principle, Marx's 'to each according to his needs'
marks.source: Aristotle, NE V.3 1131a; Rawls 1971 section 13; Sen 1979; Marx, Gotha

marks.gloss: what someone gets of what there is: the portion of the harvest, the wage packet, the dividend, the inheritance, the ration, the benefit
marks.source: Aristotle, NE V.3; Ricardo, preface

marks.gloss: a share named by its source in production: the wage of labour, the profit of stock, the rent of land, the interest of money lent; the trinity
marks.source: Smith, WN I.6; Ricardo, preface; Marx III ch. 48

marks.gloss: who holds which means and stands where in the division of labour before any product is shared: the land owned, the capital owned, the job held, the class position; Marx's distribution of the instruments of production and of persons among the branches
marks.source: Marx, Introduction of 1857 section 2; Rawls 1971 (the basic structure); Hacker 2011 (predistribution)

marks.gloss: the share given without price and received under an obligation to return: the food shared in the household, the present, the alms, the potlatch; apportioning by reciprocity
marks.source: Mauss 1925; Sahlins 1972 ch. 5; Polanyi 1957

marks.gloss: the share collected by a center and apportioned from it: the tax and the benefit, the tribute and the provision, the temple's granary, the pension; and the setting-right of a past wrong, restitution, the jubilee; apportioning by a center
marks.source: Polanyi 1944 ch. 4, 1957; Rawls 1971 section 43; Nozick 1974 ch. 7 (rectification)

marks.gloss: the share got by trading at a price: the wage for the labour, the price for the crop, the rent for the room; apportioning by exchange, without a center, through many bargains
marks.source: Polanyi 1957; Smith, WN I.7; Hayek 1976 ch. 10 (the catallaxy)

marks.gloss: the distribution as a state of the whole: the Lorenz curve, the top decile's share, the Gini, the shares summed, those with nothing counted among them; Nozick's end-state
marks.source: Piketty 2013; Atkinson 2015; Nozick 1974 ch. 7

axioms: Every share is someone's, by a title; what is no one's by any title is not yet distributed.
The measure of a right share is not read off from the shares: what one gets does not say what one should get.
Before the product is shared, the means and the positions of producing are already held; the second apportioning follows the first.
Where wealth accumulates the distribution makes its own excluded: a share of nothing is a point of the pattern.
A share got by gift, by a center or by trade is a share all the same: the form of the apportioning does not change what is apportioned.
cast.subject: Distribution: the apportioning of what is produced, and of the means and positions of producing, among the persons and classes of a society: the title by which a share is owed, the measure by which it is right, the share itself and the share by its source, the holding that comes before any sharing, the three forms the apportioning takes (the gift, the center, the market), and the result for the whole; read from Aristotle, NE V.3-5; Smith, Wealth of Nations I.6-8; Ricardo, Principles, preface; J. S. Mill, Principles II.1; Marx, Introduction of 1857 section 2, Capital III chs. 48 and 51, Critique of the Gotha Programme; Hegel, Philosophy of Right 199-208 and 243-245; Rawls, A Theory of Justice (1971); Nozick, Anarchy, State, and Utopia (1974) ch. 7; Sen, Equality of What? (1979); Walzer, Spheres of Justice (1983); Hayek, The Mirage of Social Justice (1976); Polanyi, The Economy as Instituted Process (1957); Mauss, The Gift (1925); Piketty, Capital in the Twenty-First Century (2013)

file.cast_by: Virgin Land, 2026-10-19, under MOLD v6, at Arman's word (the four new concepts named 2026-10-19; 'redo yourself', 2026-10-17). Every label, word and quality is a proposal until Arman ratifies it. Words re-poured as channels on 2026-10-19 at Arman's word.
premises: Distribution is poured as a concept of the economy and not as a theory of justice: the measure (the criterion of a right share) is one moment among others, as Aristotle's worth is a moment of the distribution itself; which measure is right is left to open_forks.

Polanyi's three forms of integration, reciprocity, redistribution and exchange, are taken as three moments, the gift, the redistribution and the market: three ways the apportioning shows up. The market here is the market's apportioning face (the share got at a price); its meeting face, buyer and seller, is left for the Production-Consumption edge, at Arman's word of 2026-10-19 that distribution and not exchange is the corner.

Marx's prior distribution, of the means of production and of persons among the kinds of production, is kept as a moment, the holding, though Marx calls it a moment of production; the boundary is noted in did_not_fit.

The share by its source (wage, profit, rent, interest; the functional distribution) and the share by its receiver are kept as two moments, the revenue and the share, because economics has always cut them apart.
The excluded (Hegel's rabble, the dispossessed) is not a moment: a share of nothing is a point of the pattern, and the making of the excluded is written as an axiom.

5.reason: what is received and kept is property and position for the next round: inheritance, accumulation (Piketty 2013 ch. 11; Marx I ch. 24)

6.reason: every share, placed among all, is a point of the distribution as a state (Piketty 2013; Atkinson 2015)

7.reason: a claim offered for a price is the exchange: transfer by consent (Hume, Treatise III.ii.4; Nozick 1974 ch. 7, justice in transfer; Pistor 2019 ch. 1)

8.reason: a claim given away is the gift: transfer without price (Mauss 1925; Nozick 1974 ch. 7, transfer)

9.reason: the gift received is the giver's claim to a return: to accept is to owe (Mauss 1925 ch. 1; Sahlins 1972 ch. 5)

10.reason: what is given and received is a portion: generalized reciprocity apportions the catch and the harvest (Sahlins 1972 ch. 5; Polanyi 1957)

11.reason: apportioning by exchange, for a factor, is its price: the wage struck, the rent agreed, the interest paid (Smith, WN I.7-8; Say, Traite II)

12.reason: what the center gives is a portion, what it takes is a portion removed: the ration, the benefit, the tax (Polanyi 1957; 1944 ch. 4)

marks.gloss: a lack the life does not require met: the preference for this over that, the taste for a thing, the longing before the purchase; Hegel's refined need, without a limit

marks.gloss: the getting of the thing at a cost: the purchase, the outlay from one's income, the drawing on a store; the propensity to consume in act
marks.source: Keynes, GT chs. 8-9; Miller 1998

marks.gloss: the thing put to what it is for: the shoe worn, the bread eaten, the book read, the tool used; and the user's making-do with it
marks.source: Aristotle, Politics I.9 1257a; de Certeau 1980; Agamben 2014

marks.gloss: the need met and felt as met: the pleasure of the meal, the warmth of the coat, the marginalist's utility, Augustine's frui
marks.source: Augustine, De doctrina christiana I.4; Gossen 1854; Scitovsky 1976

marks.gloss: the thing consumed to its end: eaten, worn out, burnt, spent; Say's destruction of utility

axioms: Consumption is the end of production and its beginning again: what is used up calls for making.
A need has a limit; a want has none.
Buying is not enjoying: the pleasure is in the use, or in the longing before.
Every society has a surplus it cannot use, and spends it, in glory or in catastrophe.
What one consumes says what one is: taste classifies.
cast.subject: Consumption: the using of what is made to the point of using it up: the need and the want, the spending that gets the thing, the thing put to its use, the use enjoyed, the thing worn away, and the social forms of use, taste, the style of life, and the spending that uses up without use; read from Aristotle, Politics I.9; Augustine, De doctrina christiana I.3-4; Smith, Wealth of Nations IV.8 and II.3; Say, Traite III; Hegel, Philosophy of Right 190-195; Marx, Introduction of 1857 section 2 and Capital I chs. 6 and 23; Keynes, General Theory chs. 8-10; Veblen, The Theory of the Leisure Class (1899); Bataille, The Notion of Expenditure (1933) and The Accursed Share (1949); Baudrillard, The Consumer Society (1970); Bourdieu, Distinction (1979); Campbell, The Romantic Ethic and the Spirit of Modern Consumerism (1987); Arendt, The Human Condition (1958); Agamben, The Use of Bodies (2014)

derived_check.ordering: by channel, read as directed: need -refined-> want -laid out-> spending -put to use-> use -felt-> enjoyment -settles-> taste -kept-> style -kept up-> want; style -required-> need; use -exhausted-> using-up -returns-> need, the body's circle; need -laid out-> spending; need -met-> use; taste -shown-> waste. Sides: use <-> waste. Refused: the want is required as no need; the spending is felt as no enjoyment; the waste returns as no need. Marked derived.

open_forks: Does the want pass into the need? Written does-not-hold for a single want, with Epicurus and Marcuse, and holds through the style of life, with Hegel and Marx; a second caster may write the direct way.
Does use pass into using-up for durable things? Arendt holds that work's products are used without being used up; the way is written of consumption as consumption, and the doubt is here.
Is the spending consumption's moment or the market's act? Kept as consumption's, as the outlay; the meeting of buyer and seller is at the edge.
Is the waste the essence (Bataille) or the edge? Kept as a moment and as the use's other side.
Is the limit a moment (the satiety, the enough) or a quality? Written as a quality and an axiom.
Does use need ownership (Agamben, the commons)? Written both ways: spending -> use and need -> use.
did_not_fit: The purchase as a meeting of buyer and seller: the market's, at the Production-Consumption edge.
Saving, consumption deferred: finance's.
Productive consumption, of means and of labour power: production's.
The share one consumes: distribution's.
The gift as given: distribution's; the gift enjoyed is consumption's.

Words left out because each keeps its two moments two: 'satisfies' (the thing satisfies the need: a cause and its effect stay two; the way is written as the use passing into the enjoyment); 'is for' (the thing is for the need: a purpose and what it serves stay two; the purpose is production's); 'requires' (the spending requires a share: a condition and what it conditions stay two).

is refined as.meaning: the first, refined and made social, is the second: the need as a want for this rather than that. The way the two are one: refinement (the one becomes the other by being refined).

is laid out as.meaning: the first, laid out from one's means, is the second: the lack or the longing as the outlay. The way the two are one: outlay (the one becomes the other by being spent for).

is put to use as.meaning: the first, put to its use, is the second: what is got, used, is the use. The way the two are one: putting to use (the one becomes the other by being used).

is met as.meaning: the first, met directly by what is at hand, is the second: the need met is the use. The way the two are one: meeting (the one becomes the other by being met without acquisition).

is felt as.meaning: the first, felt, is the second: the use felt is the enjoyment. The way the two are one: feeling (the one becomes the other by being felt).

is exhausted as.meaning: the first, carried to its end, is the second: the use exhausted is the using-up. The way the two are one: exhaustion (the one becomes the other by being used to the end).

returns as.meaning: the first, gone, returns as the second: the thing used up returns as the lack. The way the two are one: return (the one becomes the other by coming round again).

settles as.meaning: the first, repeated and compared, settles as the second: pleasures settle as taste. The way the two are one: settling by repetition (the one becomes the other by habit).

is kept as.meaning: the first, kept, is the second: taste kept is the style of life. The way the two are one: keeping (the one becomes the other by being held to).

is kept up as.meaning: the first, kept up, is the second: the standard kept up is the wants that keep it. The way the two are one: keeping up (the one becomes the other by being maintained).

is required as.meaning: the first, required, is the second: what the standard requires is a need. The way the two are one: requirement (the one becomes the other by being required).

is shown as.meaning: the first, shown to others, is the second: taste shown is conspicuous waste. The way the two are one: display (the one becomes the other by being shown).

is the other side of.meaning: the first and the second are the two sides of one consuming, with use and without. The way the two are one: two sides of one consuming.

0.reason: the lack, refined and made social, is desire for this rather than that (Hegel, PR 190-191; Marx 1857 section 2: consumption makes the need a want for a particular thing)

1.reason: the lack met by buying is the outlay on necessities: the bread bought (Keynes, GT ch. 8; Engel's law)

2.reason: the longing becomes the purchase (Campbell 1987 ch. 5; Keynes, GT chs. 8-9)

3.reason: what is got is put to its use (Smith, WN IV.8; Say, Traite III.1)

4.reason: the lack met directly by what is at hand, without acquisition: the shoe worn, use without ownership (Aristotle, Politics I.9; Agamben 2014 part I)

5.reason: the thing in use is the need met and felt as met (Augustine, De doctrina christiana I.4; Gossen 1854; Marshall, Principles III.6)

6.reason: the use completed is the thing consumed: eaten, worn out; Say's destruction of utility is the last moment of use (Say, Traite III.1; Arendt 1958 section 13)

7.reason: the thing gone, the lack is back: the cycle of the body, and consumption produces the need for new production (Marx 1857 section 2; Arendt 1958 section 13)

8.reason: pleasures settled and compared become taste, the preference that marks (Bourdieu 1979 ch. 3; Hume, Of the Standard of Taste; Veblen 1899 ch. 4)

9.reason: taste made durable, kept as a pattern: the standard of living, the habitus (Bourdieu 1979 ch. 3; Simmel, Philosophy of Money ch. 6; Duesenberry 1949)

10.reason: the standard kept generates the wants that keep it: relative income, the multiplication of needs (Duesenberry 1949 ch. 3; Hegel, PR 191)

11.reason: what a standard makes necessary is a need: the historical and moral element in what a worker must have (Marx I ch. 6; Hegel, PR 191)

12.reason: the display of taste is spending without use: conspicuous waste (Veblen 1899 ch. 4)

13.reason: consuming with use and consuming without are the two fates of what is consumed: utilitarian consumption and glorious expenditure (Bataille 1933; 1949 ch. 1)

14.reason: a single desire is not thereby a need; vain desires stay vain (Epicurus, Letter to Menoeceus 127; Marcuse 1964 ch. 1, false needs); a want becomes a need only through the style of life, see above

15.reason: buying is not enjoying: the pleasure is in the use, or in the longing before, and the purchase disappoints (Campbell 1987 ch. 5; Scitovsky 1976 ch. 4)

16.reason: expenditure without return answers no lack and leaves none: it is beyond need (Bataille 1933; 1949 ch. 1)

derived_check.ordering: by channel, read as directed: hoard -committed-> advance -owed-> promise -honoured-> return -kept-> hoard, a circle; return -committed-> advance; advance -comes back-> return; promise -sold on-> security -priced-> valuation -realized-> return; promise -fails-> default; promise -accepted-> hoard; valuation -counts-> hoard. open_forks: Money: a commodity (Menger) or a token of credit and law (Innes, Knapp, Ingham)? Written with the credit theory: the promise passes into the hoard.

Interest: a share of surplus value (Marx), the agio of present over future goods (Boehm-Bawerk, Fisher), or the price of parting with liquidity (Keynes)? The return is written as the advance in its later moment, which all three allow.
Is the default the promise's last moment (written, passes into) or its other side, as the forbearance is the deed's? Kept as a becoming: a promise is not made with its breaking as a side of it.
Whether the state's money and the state's debt are inside (Streeck, Vogl) or at the edge: the state's bond is a promise and is inside; the state's power to tax is distribution's.
Whether the derivative is a moment of its own (Appadurai, Esposito) or the security in a second degree: folded into the security.
Whether 'liquid' is a quality of each moment or a moment of its own (the liquidity; Keynes ch. 17; Mehrling): written as a quality.
did_not_fit: Money as a medium of exchange, the purchase now: the market's, found at the Production-Consumption edge; money appears here only as the hoard and as the unit of account, a mark.
The price of goods: the market's; finance prices claims.
Gambling: a bet with no claim on production; de Goede (2005) shows the line between it and finance is drawn, not found.
Insurance: a promise against loss; a form of the promise, not a moment.
Public finance as revenue: distribution's; the state's debt is a promise and is inside.
The firm's accounting: production's, until the firm is capitalized.

counts as.meaning: the first is the second by being counted so, in the books and in the market's reckoning. The way the two are one: counting.

0.reason: money kept becomes money committed when it is lent or invested: the same sum, now out to return as more (Marx, Capital I ch. 3 and II ch. 1: the hoard as the first form of money-capital; Keynes, GT ch. 13 on the choice between holding and lending)

1.reason: what the lender holds after advancing is the claim: the sum advanced is, in the lender's hands, a promise of its repayment (Innes 1914; Marx III ch. 21: the loan returns to its owner as a claim)

2.reason: the claim honoured is the payment with its interest: the promise kept is the return (Boehm-Bawerk, Positive Theory book I; Fisher 1930 ch. 1)

3.reason: the capital advanced comes back as more, M-M': the same value in its later moment (Marx III ch. 21; Schumpeter 1911 ch. 3)

4.reason: the money come back is money held again: the return taken as liquidity (Keynes, GT ch. 13; Marx II ch. 1)

5.reason: the return sent out again is the advance renewed: reinvestment, accumulation (Marx I ch. 24)

6.reason: a claim made transferable is the same claim in a saleable form: the mobilization of capital (Hilferding 1910 ch. 7; Marx III ch. 29)

7.reason: a claim traded has a price, and the price is the claim as the market reads its future: capitalization (Marx III ch. 29; Minsky 1986 ch. 8)

8.reason: a price realized by sale is a return, the capital gain: the speculator's gain from the valuation (Keynes, GT ch. 12; Minsky 1986)

9.reason: the promise unkept is the promise in its failing: the claim become a loss (Minsky 1992; Graeber 2011 ch. 1; Nietzsche GM II 5)

10.reason: a promise taken in payment is held as money: the bank's deposit is its promise and is the money one holds (Innes 1913, 1914; Ingham 2004 ch. 2; Mehrling 2011 ch. 1)

11.reason: money kept breeds nothing: a hoard yields no interest (Aristotle, Politics I.10 1258b, money barren; Keynes, GT ch. 17: money's own yield is nil, its liquidity premium is what holding it costs)

12.reason: a rise in the price of a claim commits no new money to anything: fictitious capital is not capital advanced (Marx III ch. 29: the market value of titles rises and falls with no change in the capital they stand for; Mazzucato 2018 ch. 5)

13.reason: the price of a tradable claim is counted as wealth held, as money would be: the portfolio marked to market stands beside cash on the balance sheet (Marx III ch. 29: the titles counted as capital; Nitzan and Bichler 2009 ch. 9)

marks.gloss: what the making is for, held as a form before the work: the plan of the house, the recipe, the blueprint, the order received; the form in the maker before it is in the matter
marks.source: Aristotle, Metaphysics Z.7 1032b; Marx, Capital I ch. 7 (the architect and the bee)

marks.gloss: the ability to make, had before it is used: the skill, the labour power, the fertility of the land, the machine standing idle; a power of contraries, to make or not
marks.source: Aristotle, Metaphysics Theta.3-8; Marx I ch. 6 (labour power); Georgescu-Roegen 1971 (funds)

marks.gloss: what the work is done on: the ore, the timber, the half-made part, the data set; nature as it enters the making, and past product entering again
marks.source: Marx I ch. 7 (the object of labour); Aristotle, Physics I.7

marks.gloss: the activity itself, purposeful and in time: the hand moving, the pump worked, the code written, the field ploughed
marks.source: Marx I ch. 7; Hegel, PR 196; Arendt 1958 ch. 3

marks.gloss: the working of many as one producer: the pin factory's eighteen operations, the assembly line, the collective worker, the general intellect
marks.source: Smith, WN I.1; Marx I ch. 13; Grundrisse, the fragment on machines

marks.gloss: what stands between the worker and the material and carries past work into the present one: the tool, the machine, the factory, the road; dead labour put to use
marks.source: Marx I chs. 7, 15; Simondon 1958; Sraffa 1960

marks.gloss: what the making leaves: the thing made or the service rendered, the use-value, the harvest, the house; labour objectified, at rest
marks.source: Marx I ch. 7; Hegel, Phenomenology 195; Say, Traite I.1 (utility created)

marks.gloss: what the making leaves beyond what it used up: the harvest beyond the seed and the sowers' food, the net product, surplus value in the capitalist form
marks.source: Quesnay 1758; Sraffa 1960 ch. 2; Marx I ch. 9

marks.gloss: the making again of the conditions of making: the seed kept and sown, the means replaced, the makers fed, raised and rested; the unpaid work of the household
marks.source: Marx I ch. 23; Federici 2004; Bhattacharya ed. 2017

axioms: Nothing is made without being worked: a power unexercised and a plan unexecuted make nothing.
What is made outlasts the making; what is used up in making it does not.
Every making uses up some of what was made before: production is by means of products.
The makers must be made again: there is no production without reproduction.
The surplus is what the making leaves beyond what it used; where there is none, the making only repeats itself.
cast.subject: Production: the making of what is used: a purpose and a capacity to make, work done on a material with instruments, the working of many as one producer, the product that outlasts the act, the surplus beyond what the making used up, and the renewal of the conditions of making; read from Aristotle, NE VI.4, Physics II.3, Metaphysics Theta; Smith, Wealth of Nations I.1-3 and II.3; Hegel, Phenomenology 190-196 and Philosophy of Right 196-198; Marx, Capital I chs. 7, 13-15, 23-24 and the Grundrisse; Quesnay, Tableau (1758); Sraffa, Production of Commodities by Means of Commodities (1960); Schumpeter 1911 ch. 2; Arendt, The Human Condition (1958); Georgescu-Roegen 1971; Federici, Caliban and the Witch (2004)

file.concept: Production (working name; the corner's name is Arman's to type)
file.cast_by: Virgin Land, 2026-10-19, under MOLD v6, at Arman's word (the four new concepts named 2026-10-19; 'redo yourself', 2026-10-17). Every label, word and quality is a proposal until Arman ratifies it. Words re-poured as channels on 2026-10-19 at Arman's word.
premises: Marx's labour process (purposeful activity, the object of labour, the instruments) is taken as the invariant of the concept, and the mode of production as its variation, carried in the subject matter and not as a moment.
Cooperation (the division of labour) is kept as a moment and not as a quality of the working, because Smith and Marx treat the working of many as one producer as a productive power no individual has.
Reproduction, the making again of the makers and the means, is kept as a moment (Marx I ch. 23; Federici), not left at the edge as the household.
Innovation (Schumpeter's new combination) is not a moment: it is production changed, and the change is written as a mark on the concept's history, with the entrepreneur in open_forks.
Every relation names a way one moment is the next, under Arman's rule of 2026-10-17 as MOLD v6 carries it; words that keep two moments two ('requires', 'produces', 'belongs to') are in did_not_fit.

Words re-poured on 2026-10-19 at Arman's word (14:0x): a way-word that says only that the one becomes the other ('passes into', 'runs as') is too general and says nothing of HOW; every word must name its channel, the specified path by which the first is the second. So each tuple's word is now its channel, and the signature lists the channels. Moments, glosses, qualities, tuples, polarities, reasons and axioms are unchanged from the pour of 13:4x, which stays in casts/mold-v6_2026-10-19 as the record. MOLD v6 section 3 step 4 asks for words few and general; Arman's word overrides it for this run.

derived_check.ordering: by channel, read as directed: purpose -carried out-> working; capacity -exercised-> working -fixed-> product -consumed-> reproduction -renewed-> capacity, a circle; working -divided-> cooperation -mechanized-> instrument; product -put to work-> instrument; product -left over-> surplus -invested-> instrument; material -worked into-> product; working -settles-> capacity. Refused: the purpose and the capacity are fixed as no product; the instrument is left over as no surplus. Marked derived.

open_forks: Does the instrument pass into the surplus? Written does-not-hold with Marx; the production function (Wicksteed, Cobb and Douglas) and Sraffa's refusal to attribute the surplus to any factor are the other readings.
Is the mode of production a moment or the frame of all the moments? Carried as the frame; a second caster may admit it as a moment with its ways.
Is innovation (Schumpeter's new combination) a moment of production, or finance's doing through credit? Not written; the entrepreneur has no moment here.
Is nature a co-producer (Moore 2015, ecological economics) or the material only? Written as the material; nature untouched is the edge.
Is a service a product (Say) or an action with no product (Aristotle's praxis, Arendt)? Written as a product; the quality 'lasts beyond the act' carries the difference.
Is cooperation a moment or a quality of the working? Kept as a moment (see premises).
did_not_fit: The sale of the product: the market's, at the Production-Consumption edge.
The distribution of the product and of the means: distribution's; Marx's prior distribution is the contested boundary.
The consumption of the product: consumption's, except productive consumption, which is the reproduction here.
Making money: finance's.
Art as making in the aesthetic sense: adjacent; a product that is not used.
Action (praxis), the other concept of doing: no corner of this run.
Nature untouched: the edge; nature worked is the material.

Words left out because each keeps its two moments two: 'requires' (the working requires the capacity: a condition and what it conditions stay two; the way is written as the capacity passing into the working); 'produces' (the capacity produces the product: a cause and its effect stay two; the way runs through the working); 'belongs to' (the product belongs to the maker: distribution's title, not a way of production); 'is made of' (the product is made of the material: written instead as the material passing into the product, the matter persisting through the form).

is carried out as.meaning: the first, carried out, is the second: the plan in the hands is the working. The way the two are one: execution (the one becomes the other by being carried out).

is exercised as.meaning: the first, exercised, is the second: the power in act is the working. The way the two are one: exercise (the one becomes the other by being exercised).

is worked into.meaning: the first, worked, is the second: the same matter in a new form, the ore in the iron. The way the two are one: working of matter (the one becomes the other by being worked, the matter persisting).

is fixed as.meaning: the first, fixed in a thing, is the second: labour fixes itself in the product. The way the two are one: fixing (the one becomes the other by being fixed in a thing).

is divided as.meaning: the first, divided among many and joined, is the second: the working of many as one producer. The way the two are one: division of labour (the one becomes the other by being divided and joined).

settles as.meaning: the first, repeated, settles as the second: labour settles as skill. The way the two are one: settling by repetition (the one becomes the other by habit).

is mechanized as.meaning: the first, fixed in a mechanism, is the second: the divided working as the machine. The way the two are one: mechanization (the one becomes the other by being built into a mechanism).

is put to work as.meaning: the first, put to work in a further making, is the second: the product as means. The way the two are one: putting to work (the one becomes the other by being used in making).

is consumed as.meaning: the first, consumed to replace what the making used up, is the second: the product as the renewal of the conditions of making. The way the two are one: productive consumption (the one becomes the other by being used up in renewal).

is left over as.meaning: the first, beyond what replaces the used-up, is the second: the product left over is the surplus. The way the two are one: being left over (the one is the other as what remains after replacement).

is invested as.meaning: the first, invested, is the second: the surplus as new means of production. The way the two are one: investment (the one becomes the other by being invested).

is renewed as.meaning: the first, renewing the makers and the means, is the second: reproduction as the capacity to make again. The way the two are one: renewal (the one becomes the other by being made again).

0.reason: the form held in the maker becomes the forming: the plan is realized in the hands (Aristotle, Metaphysics Z.7 1032b; Marx I ch. 7: the result existed ideally at the beginning)

1.reason: the power exercised is the power in act: labour power spent is labour (Aristotle, Metaphysics Theta.6-8; Marx I ch. 7)

2.reason: the stuff worked is the thing made, the same matter in a new form: the ore is the iron, the timber the table (Aristotle, Physics I.7; Marx I ch. 7)

3.reason: the activity, finished, is the thing made: labour objectified, in a state of rest (Hegel, Phenomenology 195; Marx I ch. 7)

4.reason: the working of one, divided and joined with others', is the working of many as one producer (Smith, WN I.1; Marx I ch. 13)

5.reason: labour settles into skill: the worker is made by working, as the just by just acts (Marx I ch. 7: the worker develops the powers that slumber in him; Aristotle NE II.1 by analogy)

6.reason: the divided working, fixed in a mechanism, is the machine: the collective worker's operations objectified (Marx I ch. 15 section 1; Hegel, PR 198)

7.reason: a thing made becomes a means of further making: past labour as dead labour, commodities by means of commodities (Marx I ch. 7; Sraffa 1960 ch. 1)

8.reason: the product used to replace what the making used up is the conditions of making renewed: the seed sown again, the wage that feeds the maker (Marx I ch. 23; Quesnay 1758)

9.reason: the product beyond what replaces the used-up is the surplus: the harvest beyond seed and sustenance, the net product (Quesnay 1758; Sraffa 1960 ch. 2; Marx I ch. 9)

10.reason: the surplus invested is new means of production: accumulation (Marx I ch. 24; Sraffa 1960)

11.reason: the makers fed, raised and rested, and the means replaced, are the capacity to make again (Marx I ch. 23; Federici 2004 ch. 2)

12.reason: a plan is not the thing: the form in the maker becomes the form in the matter only through the making (Aristotle, Metaphysics Z.7; Marx I ch. 7: the architect must build)

13.reason: a power unexercised makes nothing: the builder who does not build has built nothing (Aristotle, Metaphysics Theta.3 against the Megarians; Theta.8)

14.reason: the machine transfers its own worth to the product and adds nothing beyond it; the surplus is the working's, not the means' (Marx I ch. 8; disputed, see open_forks)

marks.gloss: that by which a share is owed to someone: ownership, a contract, membership, need, desert; the entitlement in Nozick's sense, this person's claim to this portion
marks.source: Nozick 1974 ch. 7; Hume, Treatise III.ii.2-4; Locke, Second Treatise ch. 5

marks.gloss: the standard by which shares are right shares: worth, need, equality, contribution, luck; Aristotle's axia, Rawls's difference principle, Marx's 'to each according to his needs'
marks.source: Aristotle, NE V.3 1131a; Rawls 1971 section 13; Sen 1979; Marx, Gotha

marks.gloss: what someone gets of what there is: the portion of the harvest, the wage packet, the dividend, the inheritance, the ration, the benefit
marks.source: Aristotle, NE V.3; Ricardo, preface

marks.gloss: a share named by its source in production: the wage of labour, the profit of stock, the rent of land, the interest of money lent; the trinity
marks.source: Smith, WN I.6; Ricardo, preface; Marx III ch. 48

marks.gloss: who holds which means and stands where in the division of labour before any product is shared: the land owned, the capital owned, the job held, the class position; Marx's distribution of the instruments of production and of persons among the branches
marks.source: Marx, Introduction of 1857 section 2; Rawls 1971 (the basic structure); Hacker 2011 (predistribution)

marks.gloss: the share given without price and received under an obligation to return: the food shared in the household, the present, the alms, the potlatch; apportioning by reciprocity
marks.source: Mauss 1925; Sahlins 1972 ch. 5; Polanyi 1957

marks.gloss: the share collected by a center and apportioned from it: the tax and the benefit, the tribute and the provision, the temple's granary, the pension; and the setting-right of a past wrong, restitution, the jubilee; apportioning by a center
marks.source: Polanyi 1944 ch. 4, 1957; Rawls 1971 section 43; Nozick 1974 ch. 7 (rectification)

marks.gloss: the share got by trading at a price: the wage for the labour, the price for the crop, the rent for the room; apportioning by exchange, without a center, through many bargains
marks.source: Polanyi 1957; Smith, WN I.7; Hayek 1976 ch. 10 (the catallaxy)

marks.gloss: the distribution as a state of the whole: the Lorenz curve, the top decile's share, the Gini, the shares summed, those with nothing counted among them; Nozick's end-state
marks.source: Piketty 2013; Atkinson 2015; Nozick 1974 ch. 7

axioms: Every share is someone's, by a title; what is no one's by any title is not yet distributed.
The measure of a right share is not read off from the shares: what one gets does not say what one should get.
Before the product is shared, the means and the positions of producing are already held; the second apportioning follows the first.
Where wealth accumulates the distribution makes its own excluded: a share of nothing is a point of the pattern.
A share got by gift, by a center or by trade is a share all the same: the form of the apportioning does not change what is apportioned.
cast.subject: Distribution: the apportioning of what is produced, and of the means and positions of producing, among the persons and classes of a society: the title by which a share is owed, the measure by which it is right, the share itself and the share by its source, the holding that comes before any sharing, the three forms the apportioning takes (the gift, the center, the market), and the result for the whole; read from Aristotle, NE V.3-5; Smith, Wealth of Nations I.6-8; Ricardo, Principles, preface; J. S. Mill, Principles II.1; Marx, Introduction of 1857 section 2, Capital III chs. 48 and 51, Critique of the Gotha Programme; Hegel, Philosophy of Right 199-208 and 243-245; Rawls, A Theory of Justice (1971); Nozick, Anarchy, State, and Utopia (1974) ch. 7; Sen, Equality of What? (1979); Walzer, Spheres of Justice (1983); Hayek, The Mirage of Social Justice (1976); Polanyi, The Economy as Instituted Process (1957); Mauss, The Gift (1925); Piketty, Capital in the Twenty-First Century (2013)

file.cast_by: Virgin Land, 2026-10-19, under MOLD v6, at Arman's word (the four new concepts named 2026-10-19; 'redo yourself', 2026-10-17). Every label, word and quality is a proposal until Arman ratifies it. Words re-poured as channels on 2026-10-19 at Arman's word.
premises: Distribution is poured as a concept of the economy and not as a theory of justice: the measure (the criterion of a right share) is one moment among others, as Aristotle's worth is a moment of the distribution itself; which measure is right is left to open_forks.

Polanyi's three forms of integration, reciprocity, redistribution and exchange, are taken as three moments, the gift, the redistribution and the market: three ways the apportioning shows up. The market here is the market's apportioning face (the share got at a price); its meeting face, buyer and seller, is left for the Production-Consumption edge, at Arman's word of 2026-10-19 that distribution and not exchange is the corner.

Marx's prior distribution, of the means of production and of persons among the kinds of production, is kept as a moment, the holding, though Marx calls it a moment of production; the boundary is noted in did_not_fit.

The share by its source (wage, profit, rent, interest; the functional distribution) and the share by its receiver are kept as two moments, the revenue and the share, because economics has always cut them apart.
The excluded (Hegel's rabble, the dispossessed) is not a moment: a share of nothing is a point of the pattern, and the making of the excluded is written as an axiom.

Every relation names a way one moment is the next, under Arman's rule of 2026-10-17 as MOLD v6 carries it; words that keep two moments two ('deserves', 'determines', 'is owed to', 'requires') are in did_not_fit.

derived_check.ordering: by channel, read as directed: measure -applied-> title -honoured-> share -kept-> holding -owned-> title, a circle; holding -paid-> revenue -received-> share; title -traded-> market -priced-> revenue; title -given-> gift -owed-> title, a loop of two; gift -received-> share; measure -applied-> redistribution -paid-> share; share -tallied-> pattern. Refused: the market, the pattern and the share are applied as no measure or title; the gift is traded as no market. Marked derived.

open_forks: Does the market pass into the measure? Written does-not-hold with Hayek and Walzer; Clark 1899 holds that each factor's marginal product is its just share, so the market's outcome is the measure.

Patterned or historical: Rawls makes claims from the measure applied to the basic structure, Nozick from titles by acquisition and transfer; both are written (measure -> title; holding -> title), and only the pattern as a source of claims is refused.
Are the revenue and the share one moment seen twice? Kept as two (see premises).
Is the pattern a moment or a derived reading of the shares? Kept as a moment, since inequality is a way the apportioning shows up (Piketty), with the doubt noted.
Is the excluded a moment? Written as an axiom.
Is the market here the classical exchange? Only its apportioning face; whether the market's meeting face is found at the Production-Consumption edge is to be seen at the pour of that midpoint.
Scope: the household, the state, or the world (Pogge, Beitz)? Not fixed by the cast.
did_not_fit: The sale as a meeting of buyer and seller, and the price as the market's own act: at the Production-Consumption edge; here the market is apportioning by exchange only.
The production of what is shared: production's; the holding (Marx's prior distribution) is the contested boundary, kept here.
The consumption of the share: consumption's.
Recognition and status apart from shares (Fraser 1995): outside.
Charity as a virtue: outside; as a transfer, the gift.

Words left out because each keeps its two moments two: 'deserves' and 'earns' (the person's worth and the portion stay two; the way is written as the measure passing into the title); 'determines' (production determines distribution: a cause and its effect stay two; the way is written as the holding passing into the revenue); 'is owed to' (the share and its claimant stay two; that is the title's gloss, not a word); 'requires' (redistribution requires a center: a condition and what it conditions stay two).

is applied as.meaning: the first, applied to a person or to the whole, is the second: the standard as a claim, or as the center's taking and giving. The way the two are one: application (the one becomes the other by being applied).

is owned as.meaning: the first, owned, is the second: what is held is the holder's claim. The way the two are one: ownership (the one becomes the other by being owned).

is paid as.meaning: the first, paid out, is the second: the holding paid out as its revenue; the center's provision paid out as a portion. The way the two are one: payment (the one becomes the other by being paid out).

is honoured as.meaning: the first, honoured, is the second: the claim honoured is the portion. The way the two are one: honouring (the one becomes the other by being met).

is received as.meaning: the first, received, is the second: the wage received, the gift received, is the person's portion. The way the two are one: receipt (the one becomes the other by being received).

is kept as.meaning: the first, kept, is the second: the share kept is property and position for the next round. The way the two are one: keeping (the one becomes the other by being held).

is tallied as.meaning: the first, tallied with all the others, is the second: the shares tallied are the pattern. The way the two are one: tallying (the one becomes the other by being counted together).

is traded as.meaning: the first, offered for a price, is the second: the claim traded is the exchange. The way the two are one: trade (the one becomes the other by being exchanged at a price).

is given as.meaning: the first, given without price, is the second: the claim given away is the gift. The way the two are one: giving (the one becomes the other by being given).

is owed as.meaning: the first, owed back, is the second: the gift received is the giver's claim to a return. The way the two are one: owing (the one becomes the other by being owed).

is priced as.meaning: the first, priced in the bargain, is the second: apportioning by exchange, for a factor, is its revenue. The way the two are one: pricing (the one becomes the other by being priced).

0.reason: the standard, applied to a person, is that person's claim: by worth the office, by need the ration (Aristotle, NE V.3 1131a; Rawls 1971 section 13)

1.reason: what one holds is one's claim: the land owned is the title to its rent; original acquisition (Locke, Second Treatise 27; Nozick 1974 ch. 7, justice in acquisition)

2.reason: a position in production, when the product is divided, is a source of revenue: the capital held returns as profit, the labour as wage, the land as rent (Smith, WN I.6; Marx III ch. 51)

3.reason: the claim honoured is the portion (Aristotle, NE V.3; Nozick 1974 ch. 7)

4.reason: the wage paid and the rent received are the person's portion (Smith, WN I.6; Ricardo, preface)

5.reason: what is received and kept is property and position for the next round: inheritance, accumulation (Piketty 2013 ch. 11; Marx I ch. 24)

6.reason: every share, placed among all, is a point of the distribution as a state (Piketty 2013; Atkinson 2015)

7.reason: a claim offered for a price is the exchange: transfer by consent (Hume, Treatise III.ii.4; Nozick 1974 ch. 7, justice in transfer; Pistor 2019 ch. 1)

8.reason: a claim given away is the gift: transfer without price (Mauss 1925; Nozick 1974 ch. 7, transfer)

9.reason: the gift received is the giver's claim to a return: to accept is to owe (Mauss 1925 ch. 1; Sahlins 1972 ch. 5)

10.reason: what is given and received is a portion: generalized reciprocity apportions the catch and the harvest (Sahlins 1972 ch. 5; Polanyi 1957)

11.reason: apportioning by exchange, for a factor, is its price: the wage struck, the rent agreed, the interest paid (Smith, WN I.7-8; Say, Traite II)

12.reason: what the center gives is a portion, what it takes is a portion removed: the ration, the benefit, the tax (Polanyi 1957; 1944 ch. 4)

13.reason: the standard applied to the whole is the taking and giving by a center: taxation by ability, provision by need (Rawls 1971 section 43; Polanyi 1957)

14.reason: the market's outcome is not thereby the standard of a right share: no one distributes in a catallaxy, so its results are neither just nor unjust (Hayek 1976 ch. 9; Walzer 1983 ch. 4; Clark 1899 holds the opposite, see open_forks)

15.reason: a state of the whole gives no one a claim; a pattern is not an entitlement (Nozick 1974 ch. 7: liberty upsets patterns)

16.reason: what one gets does not say what one should get; the standard is not read off the shares (Hume, Treatise III.i.1; Aristotle, NE V.3: the shares follow worth, not worth the shares)

17.reason: the obligation to return is not a sale at a price; reciprocity is not exchange (Mauss 1925, conclusion; Polanyi 1957; Walzer 1983 ch. 4, blocked exchanges)

marks.gloss: a lack the body or the life requires met: hunger, cold, shelter, the child's milk; natural at its root, social in its form; met, it is over until it returns
marks.source: Hegel, PR 190; Marx 1857 section 2; Epicurus, Letter to Menoeceus 127

marks.gloss: a lack the life does not require met: the preference for this over that, the taste for a thing, the longing before the purchase; Hegel's refined need, without a limit
marks.source: Hegel, PR 191; Campbell 1987 ch. 5; the marginalists (preference)

marks.gloss: the getting of the thing at a cost: the purchase, the outlay from one's income, the drawing on a store; the propensity to consume in act
marks.source: Keynes, GT chs. 8-9; Miller 1998

marks.gloss: the thing put to what it is for: the shoe worn, the bread eaten, the book read, the tool used; and the user's making-do with it
marks.source: Aristotle, Politics I.9 1257a; de Certeau 1980; Agamben 2014

marks.gloss: the need met and felt as met: the pleasure of the meal, the warmth of the coat, the marginalist's utility, Augustine's frui
marks.source: Augustine, De doctrina christiana I.4; Gossen 1854; Scitovsky 1976

marks.gloss: the thing consumed to its end: eaten, worn out, burnt, spent; Say's destruction of utility

axioms: Consumption is the end of production and its beginning again: what is used up calls for making.
A need has a limit; a want has none.
Buying is not enjoying: the pleasure is in the use, or in the longing before.
Every society has a surplus it cannot use, and spends it, in glory or in catastrophe.
What one consumes says what one is: taste classifies.
cast.subject: Consumption: the using of what is made to the point of using it up: the need and the want, the spending that gets the thing, the thing put to its use, the use enjoyed, the thing worn away, and the social forms of use, taste, the style of life, and the spending that uses up without use; read from Aristotle, Politics I.9; Augustine, De doctrina christiana I.3-4; Smith, Wealth of Nations IV.8 and II.3; Say, Traite III; Hegel, Philosophy of Right 190-195; Marx, Introduction of 1857 section 2 and Capital I chs. 6 and 23; Keynes, General Theory chs. 8-10; Veblen, The Theory of the Leisure Class (1899); Bataille, The Notion of Expenditure (1933) and The Accursed Share (1949); Baudrillard, The Consumer Society (1970); Bourdieu, Distinction (1979); Campbell, The Romantic Ethic and the Spirit of Modern Consumerism (1987); Arendt, The Human Condition (1958); Agamben, The Use of Bodies (2014)

premises: Need and want are kept as two moments: the lack the life requires met, and the lack it does not; Hegel's refinement of need and Marx's historical element are written as ways between them, through the style of life, not as their identity.

The spending (the outlay from one's share) is kept as consumption's own act toward the market, following Keynes's propensity to consume; the purchase as a meeting of buyer and seller is left for the Production-Consumption edge.
Bataille's expenditure without return is kept as a moment, the waste, and as the other side of the use: consuming with use and consuming without are two sides of one consuming of the surplus.
The limit of need (Aristotle, Gossen, sufficiency) is written as an axiom and as a quality, not as a moment.
Every relation names a way one moment is the next, under Arman's rule of 2026-10-17 as MOLD v6 carries it; words that keep two moments two ('satisfies', 'is for', 'requires') are in did_not_fit.

Words re-poured on 2026-10-19 at Arman's word (14:0x): a way-word that says only that the one becomes the other ('passes into', 'runs as') is too general and says nothing of HOW; every word must name its channel, the specified path by which the first is the second. So each tuple's word is now its channel, and the signature lists the channels. Moments, glosses, qualities, tuples, polarities, reasons and axioms are unchanged from the pour of 13:4x, which stays in casts/mold-v6_2026-10-19 as the record. MOLD v6 section 3 step 4 asks for words few and general; Arman's word overrides it for this run.

derived_check.ordering: by channel, read as directed: need -refined-> want -laid out-> spending -put to use-> use -felt-> enjoyment -settles-> taste -kept-> style -kept up-> want; style -required-> need; use -exhausted-> using-up -returns-> need, the body's circle; need -laid out-> spending; need -met-> use; taste -shown-> waste. Sides: use <-> waste. Refused: the want is required as no need; the spending is felt as no enjoyment; the waste returns as no need. Marked derived.

open_forks: Does the want pass into the need? Written does-not-hold for a single want, with Epicurus and Marcuse, and holds through the style of life, with Hegel and Marx; a second caster may write the direct way.
Does use pass into using-up for durable things? Arendt holds that work's products are used without being used up; the way is written of consumption as consumption, and the doubt is here.
Is the spending consumption's moment or the market's act? Kept as consumption's, as the outlay; the meeting of buyer and seller is at the edge.
Is the waste the essence (Bataille) or the edge? Kept as a moment and as the use's other side.
Is the limit a moment (the satiety, the enough) or a quality? Written as a quality and an axiom.
Does use need ownership (Agamben, the commons)? Written both ways: spending -> use and need -> use.
did_not_fit: The purchase as a meeting of buyer and seller: the market's, at the Production-Consumption edge.
Saving, consumption deferred: finance's.
Productive consumption, of means and of labour power: production's.
The share one consumes: distribution's.
The gift as given: distribution's; the gift enjoyed is consumption's.

Words left out because each keeps its two moments two: 'satisfies' (the thing satisfies the need: a cause and its effect stay two; the way is written as the use passing into the enjoyment); 'is for' (the thing is for the need: a purpose and what it serves stay two; the purpose is production's); 'requires' (the spending requires a share: a condition and what it conditions stay two).

is refined as.meaning: the first, refined and made social, is the second: the need as a want for this rather than that. The way the two are one: refinement (the one becomes the other by being refined).

is laid out as.meaning: the first, laid out from one's means, is the second: the lack or the longing as the outlay. The way the two are one: outlay (the one becomes the other by being spent for).

is put to use as.meaning: the first, put to its use, is the second: what is got, used, is the use. The way the two are one: putting to use (the one becomes the other by being used).

is met as.meaning: the first, met directly by what is at hand, is the second: the need met is the use. The way the two are one: meeting (the one becomes the other by being met without acquisition).

is felt as.meaning: the first, felt, is the second: the use felt is the enjoyment. The way the two are one: feeling (the one becomes the other by being felt).

is exhausted as.meaning: the first, carried to its end, is the second: the use exhausted is the using-up. The way the two are one: exhaustion (the one becomes the other by being used to the end).

returns as.meaning: the first, gone, returns as the second: the thing used up returns as the lack. The way the two are one: return (the one becomes the other by coming round again).

settles as.meaning: the first, repeated and compared, settles as the second: pleasures settle as taste. The way the two are one: settling by repetition (the one becomes the other by habit).

is kept as.meaning: the first, kept, is the second: taste kept is the style of life. The way the two are one: keeping (the one becomes the other by being held to).

is kept up as.meaning: the first, kept up, is the second: the standard kept up is the wants that keep it. The way the two are one: keeping up (the one becomes the other by being maintained).

is required as.meaning: the first, required, is the second: what the standard requires is a need. The way the two are one: requirement (the one becomes the other by being required).

is shown as.meaning: the first, shown to others, is the second: taste shown is conspicuous waste. The way the two are one: display (the one becomes the other by being shown).

is the other side of.meaning: the first and the second are the two sides of one consuming, with use and without. The way the two are one: two sides of one consuming.

0.reason: the lack, refined and made social, is desire for this rather than that (Hegel, PR 190-191; Marx 1857 section 2: consumption makes the need a want for a particular thing)

1.reason: the lack met by buying is the outlay on necessities: the bread bought (Keynes, GT ch. 8; Engel's law)

2.reason: the longing becomes the purchase (Campbell 1987 ch. 5; Keynes, GT chs. 8-9)

3.reason: what is got is put to its use (Smith, WN IV.8; Say, Traite III.1)

4.reason: the lack met directly by what is at hand, without acquisition: the shoe worn, use without ownership (Aristotle, Politics I.9; Agamben 2014 part I)

5.reason: the thing in use is the need met and felt as met (Augustine, De doctrina christiana I.4; Gossen 1854; Marshall, Principles III.6)

6.reason: the use completed is the thing consumed: eaten, worn out; Say's destruction of utility is the last moment of use (Say, Traite III.1; Arendt 1958 section 13)

7.reason: the thing gone, the lack is back: the cycle of the body, and consumption produces the need for new production (Marx 1857 section 2; Arendt 1958 section 13)

8.reason: pleasures settled and compared become taste, the preference that marks (Bourdieu 1979 ch. 3; Hume, Of the Standard of Taste; Veblen 1899 ch. 4)

9.reason: taste made durable, kept as a pattern: the standard of living, the habitus (Bourdieu 1979 ch. 3; Simmel, Philosophy of Money ch. 6; Duesenberry 1949)

10.reason: the standard kept generates the wants that keep it: relative income, the multiplication of needs (Duesenberry 1949 ch. 3; Hegel, PR 191)

11.reason: what a standard makes necessary is a need: the historical and moral element in what a worker must have (Marx I ch. 6; Hegel, PR 191)

12.reason: the display of taste is spending without use: conspicuous waste (Veblen 1899 ch. 4)

13.reason: consuming with use and consuming without are the two fates of what is consumed: utilitarian consumption and glorious expenditure (Bataille 1933; 1949 ch. 1)

14.reason: a single desire is not thereby a need; vain desires stay vain (Epicurus, Letter to Menoeceus 127; Marcuse 1964 ch. 1, false needs); a want becomes a need only through the style of life, see above

15.reason: buying is not enjoying: the pleasure is in the use, or in the longing before, and the purchase disappoints (Campbell 1987 ch. 5; Scitovsky 1976 ch. 4)

16.reason: expenditure without return answers no lack and leaves none: it is beyond need (Bataille 1933; 1949 ch. 1)
